questions.q: Why doesn't a parameter change anything in a view on its own?
options: Because Tableau requires a live database connection to activate a parameter
Because parameters can only be Boolean data type
Because parameters can never be used in calculated fields
Because nothing references it yet — it only takes effect once a calculated field (or filter, reference line, etc.) uses its value
questions.explain: A parameter is inert by itself. The moment a calculated field references it, moving the parameter's control recalculates that field and everything built on it.

questions.q: How do you reference a parameter inside a calculated field?
options: Parameters require a special function that cannot be typed directly
You must drag the parameter onto the Marks card first
Parameters cannot be referenced inside calculated fields at all
Type its name in the formula, exactly like referencing any other field — Tableau's autocomplete offers it alongside dimensions and measures
questions.explain: You reference a parameter by name just like any dimension or measure — Tableau's calculation editor autocompletes it right alongside your other fields.

questions.q: In the worked example `IF SUM([Quantity]) < [Reorder Threshold] THEN "Reorder Now" ELSE "Stock OK" END`, what role does [Reorder Threshold] play?
options: It's a hardcoded dimension from the data source
It's the name of the calculated field itself
It's the user-adjustable input — a Range parameter the calculated field compares against
It has no effect on the calculation's result
questions.explain: [Reorder Threshold] is the parameter — the input a person controls via a slider. The calculated field is the behavior: comparing quantity on hand against whatever threshold value the parameter currently holds.

questions.q: What is the general pattern behind parameter + calculated field combinations, as this lesson frames it?
options: The calculated field must always be created before the parameter
The parameter is the input a person controls; the calculated field is the behavior — what actually happens with that input
Parameters and calculated fields cannot reference each other under any circumstance
The parameter always controls color, and the calculated field always controls size
questions.explain: This input/behavior split is the pattern reused across Lessons 65-67: a parameter supplies a user-controlled value, and a calculated field defines what happens with it.

questions.q: In the lab's `Above Target?` calculation, `SUM([Profit]) / SUM([Sales]) >= [Profit Margin Target]`, what happens when the Profit Margin Target slider moves?
options: Nothing changes because parameters cannot be used in Boolean comparisons
The calculated field must be manually rebuilt each time the slider moves
The underlying Sales and Profit data in the source is modified
The calculated field re-evaluates against the new target value, which can change which sub-categories are colored as above or below target
questions.explain: Because the calculated field references the parameter directly, every time its current value changes, the calculation re-evaluates automatically — no manual rebuild needed.
